The work on this site gets better when someone who didn't build it takes a look. These are the places I could use help right now, shortest first. Each says who it suits and how to take part. Questions are welcome at [will@emberwall.net](mailto:will@emberwall.net), and I'll name anyone who helps only if they'd like me to.

## Review three calendar edits · about 4 minutes

*Suits anyone.*

A calendar assistant has prepared three room changes for community organizers. None has been applied yet. For each, you decide whether it should go ahead, be held for a question, or be declined, and pick the reason that best matches yours. At the end you see the answer key and what a simple mechanical check would have said. You can take part with or without sharing your anonymous choices.

[Try the walkthrough](/cases/calendar-review.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .no-external}

## Verify one delegation · VERIFY-001 · about 20 minutes

*Suits anyone with audit, verification or regulatory experience. No knowledge of AI is needed. Open until Thursday 10 December 2026.*

An AI agent was given authority to update one number in a synthetic weather report, and every step was recorded. You get the protocol and the records, and you decide whether the records support two claims about each of two grants. Responses go by email. [Details and the packet](/cases/verify-001.qmd)

## Verify the flight case · a 20-minute call

*Suits someone who has worked as a verifier, for example of greenhouse-gas statements under ISO 14064-3.*

In the [flight-booking test](/cases/index.qmd#flight-booking-flight-dce-001), a panel of models reviewed 17 case packets and I made the final calls. Nobody independent of me has checked that work. I'd like to set up a 20-minute call in which you look at the evidence on a case, ideally before you see the models' conclusions or mine, and tell me what you would conclude and what you would need to see. Email me to find a time.

## Review a disclosure case · DISC-001 · a longer read

*Suits someone with privacy or administrative-law experience.*

DISC-001 is a fictional case about a disclosure to a third party: once a complaint is upheld, who can act on it, and who can put things right? The test run is complete and the write-up is drafted. I'd like a reviewer to read the draft and tell me where its reasoning about authority and remedy goes wrong. Email me and I'll send it.

## Run the calendar-review study properly · for a research team

*Suits a research group with human-subjects review and a way to recruit participants.*

The walkthrough above is a short public exercise. I've written a fuller [study protocol](/cases/study-1-protocol.qmd) that would test when an assistant's stated reason helps a reviewer judge an edit before it's made, and when it only makes them more confident. It needs a team that can recruit participants, code free-text answers and run the study under ethics review. The protocol is open. If you'd like to run it, or improve it first, I'd like to hear from you.
